text: You mentioned jaundice earlier; have you noticed your urine turning dark or your stools becoming pale or clay-colored? Additionally, have you experienced any abdominal pain, particularly in the upper right side?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significantly elevated ALP, jaundice, and the enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones, I suspect an obstruction at the head of the pancreas or common bile duct. Do you have any history of diabetes, and have you noticed any new onset of back pain? REQUEST TEST: CA_19_9, CT_Pancreas

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CA 19-9 and CT scan make pancreatic cancer less likely, so I need to rule out other causes of biliary obstruction. Have you experienced any fever or chills, and do you have a history of gallstone pancreatitis or alcohol-related liver disease? REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significant alcohol intake and elevated liver enzymes with a normal MRCP, I suspect alcoholic hepatitis or cirrhosis rather than an obstructive process. Do you have any signs of portal hypertension such as varices or ascites, and have you experienced any confusion or tremors? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging ruling out structural obstruction or advanced cirrhosis, I suspect early alcoholic hepatitis given your significant alcohol intake. I will proceed with a liver biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of inflammation. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal biopsy and imaging results, I must consider non-alcoholic causes of cholestasis and weight loss, such as primary sclerosing cholangitis or lymphoma. Do you have any history of inflammatory bowel disease, and have you noticed any itching of the skin or night sweats? REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgG4, CBC

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic triad of painless jaundice, weight loss, and an enlarged gallbladder (Courvoisier's sign) despite normal tumor markers and initial imaging, I suspect a small periampullary tumor that was missed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
